neighbours.caption: Reticulohistiocytoma. Mainly occurring in adults, this is a solitary or multiple dermal nodular lesion. Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis may present accompanied by fever, weight loss, and polyarthritis. There is a sheet-like in fi ltrate of histiocytes, including multinucleated cells, with in fl ammatory cells

Round cell liposarcoma. This tumor has sheets of rounded nuclei, some of which are vacuolated. No vascular pattern is discernible. This is regarded as the high-grade or more aggressive variant of myxoid liposarcoma, although no genetic differences between the two histologic patterns have been shown

Poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma. This is a small round cell tumor. The nuclei appear to overlap. More typical areas usually can be found by further sampling of the tumor, but immunohistochemical and genetic analysis may be required to distinguish this from other small round cell tumors
Deep compound lesion with dense inflammatory infiltrate and small glandular cysts (H&E 10x).

full.description: This is a histopathological micrograph showing a dense sheet-like proliferation of round tumor cells with numerous vacuolated nuclei. The high-power view reveals sheets of rounded cells characteristic of a round cell liposarcoma. The prominent vacuolations within the tumor cells are indicative of lipoblastic differentiation. The tissue architecture displays a high-grade malignant mesenchymal neoplasm.

blind.description: This image is a micrograph showing a dermal nodular lesion characterized by a sheet-like infiltrate of histiocytes and multinucleated cells accompanied by inflammatory cells. The tissue architecture and cellular composition are consistent with reticulohistiocytoma. Such lesions mainly occur in adults as solitary or multiple dermal nodules. The findings support the diagnosis of reticulohistiocytoma.

random.description: This is a histopathologic micrograph showing a dense proliferation of lymphoid cells with a classic "starry sky" appearance. The dark-staining sheets of malignant round cells are interspersed with numerous tangible-body macrophages containing apoptotic debris, creating the characteristic starry sky pattern. These features are highly suggestive of Burkitt lymphoma, a high-grade B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The abundant clear spaces from the macrophages stand out against the background of uniform, medium-sized tumor cells.
captions: Prostate cancer with subtle architectural and cytological atypia. In this case, the cancer glands display crowded growth pattern (a). The cancer cells have minimum nuclear enlargement and inconspicuous nucleoli (b). This focus is negative for basal cell marker p63 (c). The cancer diagnosis in such cases requires a substantial number of cancer glands and ancillary immunohistochemistry

Albumin mRNA expression is relatively specific for normal and neoplastic liver cells. B, The sense control probe is negative.
